key_insight: First-principles spin-orbit calculations show that chiral hybrid perovskites ($R$/$S$-PEA)PbI$_3$ and ($R$/$S$-NEA)PbI$_3$ host strong, chirality-dependent spin-split bands with opposite spin textures for opposite molecular handedness.
engineering_relevance: The results identify molecular choice and chiral distortion as design knobs for tuning spin splitting and circular-dichroism-related response in perovskite optoelectronic materials.
method: Performed first-principles electronic-structure calculations including spin-orbit coupling.
Compared band structures of PEA-based and NEA-based chiral 1D perovskites.
Used group-theoretical analysis for the nonsymmorphic space group $P2_12_12_1$ to explain degeneracies and band sticking.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports stronger effective valence-band-edge spin splitting in ($R$/$S$-NEA)PbI$_3$, arising from larger SOC-induced gaps and band (anti)crossings, while both compounds show pronounced splitting near band edges.
watch_item: These are theoretical predictions from idealized calculations, so the predicted spin textures and splittings still need experimental validation and may be sensitive to structural details and sample quality.
paper_title: First-principles calculations of spin-split bands in chiral hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites ($R$/$S$-PEA)PbI$_3$ and ($R$/$S$-NEA)PbI$_3$
